content: Sen-Sen, marketed as a breath perfume, was a type of breath freshener. In the early 20th century, before the health risks of tobacco were scientifically established, Sen-Sen was a commercial product designed to mask the smell of tobacco on a person’s breath and clothing. At that time, disapproval of tobacco use was primarily based on moral and personal reasons rather than health concerns. Adolescent boys, for example, would use Sen-Sen to attempt to conceal from their parents the fact that they had been smoking. This association with moral shortcomings led to Sen-Sen being referenced in the song Ya Got Trouble from the musical comedy The Music Man, where it was included in a list of moral faults. The product was also mentioned in Billy Joel's song Keeping the Faith, with the lyrics: I took a fresh pack of Luckies and a mint called Sen-Sen. Additionally, Sen-Sen appeared in literature, such as the book Their Eyes Were Watching God, where it was noted for masking not only tobacco breath but also the smell of alcohol. It was also referenced in A Tree Grows in Brooklyn, where the character Hildy O'Dair was described as using it. In Europe, a similar product aimed at female smokers was available, called tabac blond.
